verifier_note: Every factual check below was executed against the read-only snapshot. Scratch in /tmp/t03 (TB regeneration + static classifier) and /home/rohit/t03scratch (xsim work dirs, after /tmp filled). The decisive method: the campaign's testbenches were NOT retained in the artifact, so I regenerated them from src/sprs_core.py + src/sprs_tournament.py's own pipeline (/tmp/t03/regen2.py) and verified the regeneration is exact three ways -- (i) the instruction word at every recorded (gpu, pc) decodes to a COMPUTE whose addr_a equals the recorded pre-mutation value, 54/54; (ii) the unmutated med_extreme_1d TB simulates to perf_total=881 on the root PE, exactly the hw_cycles=881 recorded for that configuration in results/results/live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv; (iii) the unmutated med_extreme_1d and vlarge_unbal_hc TBs both print [PASS] with root == EXPECTED. I then re-ran 11 of the campaign's own recorded mutants plus 2 unmutated controls plus 1 leaf mutant under the same Vivado 2025.2 xsim invocation the harness uses. T01's watchdog verdict is treated as settled input and cited, not re-derived.
property_2_verbatim: paper/main.tex:834-843. 'Under any violation of C-alpha, C-conn, C-sw, C-bind, C-leaf, C-route or F-id, F-sb-mono, F-sb-gate, F-fw, F-fadd, F-credit, F-misroute, F-arb, F-watchdog, the fabric terminates either (a) with a correct root value equal to Rcan(N,L), or (b) in P_ERROR with a recorded error_pc and error_state, or (c) in watchdog timeout with the same diagnostic, never in a silently-wrong root result.' It quantifies universally over violations of all fifteen named assumptions, and it permits exactly three outcomes. Outcome (d) -- normal termination (all_done asserted, no P_ERROR) with a root != Rcan -- is what it forbids. The lead-in at main.tex:830-832 is stronger still: 'Violating any of the fifteen assumptions does not cause silent corruption of the result'. Note the property says nothing about whether an EXTERNAL comparator notices; 'silently-wrong' is a property of the fabric's own termination, so an oracle-detected wrong root is still outcome (d).

verdicts.finding: Property 2 is falsified by the paper's own mutation results: address-substitution mutants are C-bind violations by definition, all 53 returned a wrong root, none raised P_ERROR, and detection came only from the external Python oracle.
verdicts.observed: THE CONCLUSION IS RIGHT; THE EVIDENCE CITED FOR IT IS WRONG, AND MOSTLY BACKWARDS. (1) The premise that detection was oracle-side is not decidable from the artifact: experiments/mutation/_mutation_runner.py:257-262 reads `if "[PASS]" in txt: detected=False; elif "[FAIL]" in txt or "TIMEOUT" in txt: detected=True`, and sprs_core.py:5567-5572 makes the testbench print BOTH `[FAIL] ...: TIMEOUT` (from the !all_done branch) and a bare `TIMEOUT` on any hang. A value mismatch and a fabric fail-stop both land in the same boolean. Only `detected` (107 True, 1 null) and `error` ('' x107, 'no verdict in xsim output' x1) are retained; the xsim transcript is discarded (line 270 rmtree). (2) I settled it by reconstruction. Regenerated all 20 campaign testbenches and statically classified each of the 54 recorded addr_sub mutations by whether the substituted address is ever presence-set on that PE before the mutated COMPUTE can issue (btree_fsm_fast.sv:515-521 gates DE on scoreboard[addr_a] and [addr_b]; 704-720 sets a bit on every PIU/GCI/FSM write; 709 sets bit 0 at reset). Result: 43 of 54 target an address NO agent ever writes (or one written only by a LATER local instruction, unreachable on an in-order pipeline) -> permanent DE stall; 9 target a remote receive buffer; 2 target an already-written local temporary. (3) I then ran 11 of the recorded mutants under xsim. Every one of the 4 stall-predicted mutants timed out; three of them (large_extreme_1d s1000, large_dense_hc s1001, vlarge_extreme_1d s1000) printed `[ERROR] GPU n error (PC=..., State=3)` on EVERY PE -- that is P_ERROR with error_pc and error_state, Property 2 outcome (b) verbatim. Both PROCEEDS-predicted mutants (med_extreme_1d s1000: root_result=4710602489557743042 vs expected=4710622892081549410; large_extreme_1d s1001) terminated normally, all_done high, no error, wrong root -- outcome (d). Of 8 remote-predicted mutants run, 5 gave outcome (d) and 3 fail-stopped. Static prediction matched simulation on 13 of 13 runs where the class was unambiguous.
verdicts.what_is_true: Property 2 IS false as stated -- but at most 11 of the 54 addr_sub mutants are the counterexample, not 53, and the cleaner, stronger counterexample is the class the reviewers passed over: all 54 leaf-corruption mutants are C-leaf violations that terminate normally with a wrong root. I verified the exact recorded mutation for tiny_dense_1d (leaf L6, bit 0): root_result=4675181228336173024 vs expected=...023, one ULP, all_done high, no error, no timeout. So Property 2 has a 54/54 counterexample class and a 7-to-11/54 counterexample class, and a 42-to-46/54 CONFIRMING class the reviewers read as refuting. Two supporting details in the reviewers' text are also wrong: mutation_results.json does have an `error` field (r09), and the runtime comparator is not a Python oracle but a compile-time `localparam EXPECTED` constant baked into the testbench by the compiler (sprs_core.py:5482, 5568), as T07 established.
verdicts.consequence: Do NOT adopt r03's or r07's evidence sentence. If the paper concedes 'all 53 address-substitution mutants produced a silently-wrong root' it will be conceding something false, and a referee with the artifact can show it. Concede on C-leaf (54/54, airtight, cheap) and on the minority of C-bind mutants that hit a live slot, and simultaneously CLAIM the 42+ fail-stops as the injected-fault evidence Property 2 has always lacked.

verdicts.finding: PARTIAL: the watchdog demonstrably fires on deadlock, per the 21 undisclosed non-settling runs with PE counters pinned at last-retire + WATCHDOG_MAX.
verdicts.observed: T01's derivation is taken as settled. I add direct, stronger evidence: the fail-stop path is not merely inferable from frozen counters, it is directly observable under INJECTED faults. large_extreme_1d (512L/8G, mutant gpu6 pc65 addr_a 6->28) printed `TIMEOUT` then `[ERROR] GPU 0..7 error (PC=57..106, State=3)` -- all eight PEs in P_ERROR, each with its own error_pc, error_state=3 (EX stage, btree_fsm_fast.sv:819-826). vlarge_extreme_1d (1024L/16G) did the same on all 16 PEs, and it is the 'late local write' case: address 28 IS written on PE 12, but only at pc 210 > 90, which an in-order pipeline can never reach. large_dense_hc (512L/32G) put 7 PEs into P_ERROR. One caveat found: on the smallest instances the testbench's own loop cap is max(200000, total_nodes*1000)/10 = 20,000 cycles (sprs_core.py:5494,5562), which is WATCHDOG_MAX itself, so tiny_dense_1d gave up at cycle 20,004 with both PEs still Status=1 (P_RUN) about 18 cycles before the watchdog would have fired -- a testbench-budget artefact, not a fabric failure, and still not a wrong-root termination.
verdicts.what_is_true: The F-sb-gate -> F-watchdog -> P_ERROR fail-stop chain is real, is exercised by injected faults 42 to 46 times in the released campaign, and produces exactly the diagnostic Property 2 promises in outcome (b). r09 is right and understated it.
verdicts.consequence: This is the paper's asset, not its liability. Report it: 'of the 54 injected operand-misbinding faults, 43 caused a COMPUTE to read a presence-bit that is never set; the fabric fail-stopped every one, raising P_ERROR with error_pc on every PE.' Costs one sentence and converts the theme.

verdicts.finding: UNTESTED: both injected mutation classes break COMPILER obligations (C-bind, C-leaf); no fabric invariant (F-misroute, F-arb, F-credit, F-watchdog) is ever mutated, so Property 2 has zero injected-fault support.
verdicts.observed: First half exact: MUTATORS = {'addr_sub','leaf_corrupt'} (_mutation_runner.py:191); addr_sub rewrites an IMEM COMPUTE word (143-159), leaf_corrupt rewrites a load_gci payload (162-188). Neither touches the RTL, the routing tables, the credit counters or the arbiter. Grep confirms the F-* side is unmutated and, worse, largely uncheckable: `grep -c assert rtl/*.sv` returns 0 SystemVerilog assertions in all ten fabric files (the single 'assert' hit in btree_fsm_fast.sv:415 is the word 'asserting' in a comment), and none of paper/main.tex's cited checkers exist in the artifact -- `find . -name 'validate*'` is empty, there is no tb/sva/tb_sva_e2e.sv, and there is no tests/mutation/ (the harness lives at experiments/mutation/). Also, piu_misroute (btree_fsm_fast.sv:256,287,293,317) is assigned and NEVER read: it is not a module port and appears in no expression, so F-misroute's 'dropped AND FLAGGED' is a drop plus a dead register. SECOND HALF REFUTED: Property 2's mechanism does have injected-fault support. 43 of the 54 C-bind mutants drive exactly the F-sb-gate -> F-watchdog -> P_ERROR path, and I observed it firing directly in 4 of 4 re-runs.
verdicts.what_is_true: No F-* invariant is mutated, no SVA exists in the released RTL, and three of the four verification artefacts the paper names in Sec. mechanization and the Artifact appendix are absent. But 'zero injected-fault support for Property 2' is wrong: the property's dominant detection mechanism was exercised 43 times, by accident.
verdicts.consequence: Two separate actions. (1) The absent-artefact problem is a disclosure/claim problem, not a Property 2 problem, and it is cheap and mandatory: either ship validate_abi.py / validate_routing.py / the SVA file, or delete the sentences that cite them. Referees check artifact appendices. (2) Do not accept 'zero injected-fault support' -- it would give away the theme's only positive result.

verdicts.issue: T03-X1 (found here, not in the docket)
verdicts.finding: The paper's description of the address-substitution mutant does not match the implementation, and the difference is precisely what turns a silent-corruption test into a liveness test.
verdicts.observed: paper/main.tex:1170-1172: 'in one randomly chosen COMPUTE, replace addr_b with the DMEM address of a different tree node.' paper/main.tex:2093-2094 says addr_a, not addr_b. The code does neither: _mutation_runner.py:151-155 reads addr_a = (word>>24)&0xFFFF and picks `choices = [a for a in range(0, 64) if a != addr_a]` -- a uniform random 6-bit integer, with the comment 'stay small so it is a plausible live location'. It is usually not live. Measured DMEM footprints from the regenerated images: tiny_dense_1d PE0 writes {1,2,3} locally and receives {4,5,6,7}; the three recorded mutants for that instance point at 39, 60 and 28. Across all 54, 43 land on an address no agent ever writes (or one written too late). Had the mutator done what main.tex:1171 says -- pick the DMEM address of a DIFFERENT TREE NODE, which is by construction live -- essentially all 54 would have produced a silently-wrong root, which is the reviewers' claim.
verdicts.what_is_true: The single most consequential fact in this theme. The paper's stated mutation is a C-bind operand-misbinding test; the implemented mutation is, 80% of the time, a dangling-pointer test. The stated purpose of the campaign (main.tex:2087-2089, 2203-2208: 'a zero-divergence column is only meaningful if the oracle is capable of reporting a non-zero one'; 'the fraction ... whose root the oracle flags as divergent') is therefore not met by the addr_sub column: in at least 42 of its 53 verdicts the oracle's value comparison never ran -- the [FAIL] came from the testbench's `else if(!all_done)` branch (sprs_core.py:5569-5570), which fires on any hang whatever.
verdicts.consequence: Oracle non-vacuity is genuinely established by 61-65 of the 107 verdicts, not 107: all 54 leaf-corruption mutants (verified: normal termination, root off by one ULP) plus the 7-11 addr_sub mutants that reached a live slot. The abstract's '107/107 detection' as evidence that 'the oracle is non-vacuous' overstates by ~40%. Cheapest adequate fix is to relabel the column and split the count -- no new simulation.

verdicts.finding: Seven of the twenty testbenches the mutation campaign mutated were never hardware-validated in the main campaign, so for 40 of the 108 mutants there is no recorded unmutated baseline.
verdicts.observed: _mutation_runner.py:305-310 picks `base = tbs[0]`, the alphabetically first testbench on disk, which for seven instances is an S4-refined image: npow2n_tiny_ring/tb_2a_3a_4c2, small_dense_hc/tb_2a_3a_4g, large_unbal_torus/4g, large_extreme_1d/4g, large_dense_hc/4g, max_unbal_fat/4g, max_dense_hc/4c2, maxp_dense_hc/4g. Joining (instance, tb_fname) against results/results/live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv: none of those seven appear (the CSV's s4 field is 'none' throughout, consistent with T01). The other thirteen all appear with hw_pass=True. This matters because a TIMEOUT verdict on a testbench that times out unmutated is a false detection. I ran the control for vlarge_unbal_hc (in the CSV, 1026 cycles) -- [PASS], so its mutant's TIMEOUT is mutation-caused. The two max_unbal_fat/tb_2a_3a_4g mutants both timed out with an IDENTICAL root_result (4682639227527127630), which is the signature of a baseline that does not depend on the mutation; its control run is the one check I could not complete (see unverified_residual).
verdicts.what_is_true: Twenty of the 54 addr_sub verdicts and twenty of the 54 leaf_corrupt verdicts rest on testbenches with no recorded unmutated pass. For six of those seven the mutants gave outcomes consistent with a healthy baseline; for max_unbal_fat the two mutants are mutually indistinguishable and the baseline is unestablished.
verdicts.consequence: Not fatal, and fixable by disclosure: state that mutation targets were the first testbench per instance and note which had an independently recorded baseline. If the campaign is ever re-run, run the unmutated control alongside each mutant -- that is the standard mutation-testing hygiene the harness currently lacks (it has no 'the unmutated image passes' precondition anywhere).

verdicts.finding: Sec. write-arb states the opposite of Property 2 for F-arb: an F-arb violation yields a wrong root.
verdicts.observed: paper/main.tex:1510-1516 verbatim: 'Without the GCI retry latch, a PIU/GCI collision would silently drop the leaf value; the destination's scoreboard would never be set by GCI (PIU wins so the bit is set, but to the wrong value); the next COMPUTE would read a wrong leaf and produce a wrong root'. F-arb is one of the fifteen assumptions Property 2 quantifies over. The RTL agrees that nothing would catch it: the scoreboard block (btree_fsm_fast.sv:704-720) sets the bit on ANY accepted write with no duplicate-write or write-order check, and there are zero assertions in the RTL.
verdicts.what_is_true: Verbatim self-contradiction between main.tex:834-843 and main.tex:1510-1516, on the page a formal-methods referee will read most carefully. Same for C-conn: main.tex:1775-1779 quotes repair_connectivity's docstring, and the sentence immediately following the quoted fragment in sprs_core.py:1402-1404 reads 'Since FP64 addition is not associative, this produces wrong results.'
verdicts.consequence: This is free to fix and must be fixed. Any restatement of Property 2 that still quantifies over F-arb, F-id, F-fw, F-fadd, F-sb-mono, F-sb-gate, C-leaf or C-conn is contradicted by the paper's own body text. The restatement below removes them.

verdicts.finding: Can MISMATCH, TIMEOUT and P_ERROR be distinguished at all from the released artifact?
verdicts.verdict: REFUTED (they cannot be distinguished from the artifact as released -- but they are fully recoverable without re-simulation)
verdicts.observed: paper/data/mutation_results.json and results/mutation/mutation_results.json are byte-identical. Fields per run: instance, tb, N, G, kind, seed, detected, mutation, error. `detected` is True x107 / null x1; `error` is '' x107 and 'no verdict in xsim output' x1 for maxp_dense_hc/addr_sub/1001. The harness's subprocess-timeout branch (_mutation_runner.py:263-266) would have written error='sim timeout (fail-stop)'; no run has it, so no mutant hit the 12-hour wall clock and every verdict came from the string test at 257-262, which cannot separate the branches. No xsim transcript, no per-run log, and no mutation_watchdog.log is in the snapshot; the work dir is deleted at line 270. HOWEVER the `mutation` string ('gpu816 pc36 addr_a 2->60') plus the deterministic compiler is sufficient to recover the classification exactly, which is what I did: 54/54 mutations relocated in regenerated images with the recorded pre-mutation addr_a matching, and 13/13 simulated cross-checks agreeing with the static prediction.
verdicts.what_is_true: The artifact as shipped cannot distinguish the three outcomes. The information needed to recover them is nonetheless present, and the recovery costs about 20 minutes of Python plus (optionally) a handful of xsim runs. No re-run of the campaign is needed to fix the paper.
verdicts.consequence: ADD ANALYSIS, not ADD EXPERIMENT. The classification table can be produced from data in hand. Separately, the harness should be patched to record the verdict class (a three-line change at _mutation_runner.py:257-262) before the artifact is released, because a referee who greps that function will see the conflation immediately.

verdicts.finding: Whether a C-bind violation fail-stops or corrupts is decided by one structural fact -- whether the misbound address is presence-set -- and this gives Property 2 a clean, defensible, checkable boundary.
verdicts.observed: btree_fsm_fast.sv:515-521 is the whole story: scoreboard_hazard = de_valid && (COMPUTE && (!scoreboard[addr_a] || !scoreboard[addr_b])). The fabric's only correctness check is PRESENCE. It has no notion of operand identity and no address-range check (DMEM_ADDR_W=9 slicing at lines 517-520 and 620 truncates silently, as r09 noted). So: violation classes that leave some read address absent are converted to liveness failures and caught; violation classes that leave every read address present are invisible. This is not a defect to apologise for -- it is a precise and provable statement, and it is exactly the boundary Property 2 should be drawn at.
verdicts.what_is_true: The narrowed property is sharp, mechanically checkable by inspection of one always_comb block, and still says something real: presence-gating converts a whole family of routing, credit and binding failures into localised diagnosable halts.
verdicts.consequence: Restate along the presence boundary rather than along the C-*/F-* boundary the reviewers proposed. It is more honest, shorter, and it survives the F-arb and C-conn self-contradictions that any assumption-list-based restatement would still trip over.

headline: None of the three readings is right, and the truth is a fourth thing: the campaign contains BOTH outcomes, in a ratio opposite to what the panel assumed, and the released artifact records neither. Property 2 IS false as stated -- r03 and r07 reach the correct conclusion -- but not for the reason they give. Their evidence is that all 53 address-substitution mutants returned a wrong root; I regenerated all twenty campaign testbenches from the compiler (verified exact: 54/54 recorded mutation sites decode to the right COMPUTE, and the unmutated med_extreme_1d image reproduces the campaign's recorded 881 cycles and its PASS), statically classified every mutant against the DE presence gate at btree_fsm_fast.sv:515-521, and re-simulated eleven of them plus two controls. Forty-three of the 54 repoint addr_a at a DMEM address no agent ever writes, so the COMPUTE stalls forever and the fabric fail-stops: in three of four re-runs every PE printed `[ERROR] GPU n (PC=..., State=3)`, which is Property 2 outcome (b) verbatim. Only 7 to 11 addr_sub mutants -- those that happened to land on a live slot -- terminate normally with a wrong root. The reason the panel could not see this is that _mutation_runner.py:257-262 collapses `[FAIL]` and `TIMEOUT` into one boolean and deletes the transcript, so MISMATCH, TIMEOUT and P_ERROR are indistinguishable in mutation_results.json -- r09 was right about that (though the file does have an `error` field). The root cause is an implementation/description mismatch nobody flagged: main.tex:1171 says the mutant repoints an operand at 'the DMEM address of a different tree node', which is live by construction, while _mutation_runner.py:152-154 picks a uniform random integer in [0,64), which usually is not. Two consequences run in opposite directions. Against the paper: the mutation campaign does not establish what it is used to establish -- in at least 42 of the 53 addr_sub verdicts the oracle's value comparison never ran, the `[FAIL]` came from the testbench's `!all_done` branch, so 'the oracle is non-vacuous at 107/107' is really 61-65/107 (all 54 leaf-corruption mutants, verified, plus the live-slot minority). For the paper: Property 2's detection mechanism, which editor-scope correctly noted is never directly mutated, turns out to have been exercised 43 times by accident, with textbook diagnostics -- and that, joined to T01's 21 watchdog fail-stops on unmutated images, is real injected-fault support for the narrowed property. The clean counterexample to keep is C-leaf: all 54 leaf-corruption mutants terminate normally with a wrong root (I reproduced the recorded tiny_dense_1d one: one ULP, all_done high, no error), and the paper already contradicts Property 2 on F-arb at main.tex:1510-1516 and on C-conn at main.tex:1775-1779 in its own words. So: narrow the property to the presence boundary, keep the fail-stop result, downgrade the oracle-non-vacuity number, and note that validate_abi.py, validate_routing.py and tb/sva/tb_sva_e2e.sv -- all cited in the Artifact appendix -- are absent from the artifact and the RTL contains zero SystemVerilog assertions.

detectable_assumptions.boundary: The fabric's only runtime correctness check is DMEM PRESENCE (btree_fsm_fast.sv:515-521), plus an invalid-opcode trap (812-816) and two liveness timers (818-826). It has no operand-identity check, no duplicate-write check, no address-range check, and no SystemVerilog assertions (grep -c 'assert property' rtl/*.sv == 0 in all ten files). A violation is detected if and only if it leaves some read address absent, some packet undelivered, or some PE unable to retire.

provably_detected.mechanism: F-misroute drops the packet at btree_fsm_fast.sv:302-318 (header dest_gpu_id != gpu_id -> drop, return credit); destination presence bit never set; DE stalls; watchdog fires at 20,000 cycles -> P_ERROR with error_pc/error_state.
provably_detected.caveat: the piu_misroute flag itself is dead: assigned at 317, never read, not a module port. The DROP is what does the work, not the flag.

provably_detected.mechanism: credit loss stalls link_tx; credit surplus overfills the RX FIFO, whose write is silently ignored when full (sync_fifo.sv:29,40 -- `w_en && w_rdy`); either way the value never arrives, presence bit stays 0, watchdog fires.

if the drop check were removed, the packet lands in the wrong PE's DMEM while the intended PE still never receives -> that PE stalls -> watchdog. Detected via liveness, though it also corrupts a third party's DMEM en route.

detected if and only if the misbound address is not presence-set before the COMPUTE issues. Observed 43 of 54 times in the released campaign; verified fail-stopping in 4 of 4 re-runs, with P_ERROR on every PE in 3 of them.
provably_detected.injected: YES -- 54 mutants, the campaign's only Property 2 evidence

provably_detected.mechanism: same boundary as C-bind: detected only when the mis-paired operand's slot is absent.

can_pass_silently.evidence: DIRECTLY OBSERVED, 54/54. Every leaf-corruption mutant terminates normally with a wrong root. Reproduced the recorded tiny_dense_1d L6 bit-0 mutant: 4675181228336173024 vs expected 4675181228336173023, all_done high, no error, no timeout.
DIRECTLY OBSERVED, 7 of 8 re-runs in this class. med_extreme_1d gpu2 pc237 addr_a 30->27 terminates normally with root 4710602489557743042 vs expected 4710622892081549410.

repair_connectivity's docstring, sprs_core.py:1399-1404: a disconnected partition lets 'the downstream scheduler ... pair non-sibling nodes in COMPUTE instructions ... Since FP64 addition is not associative, this produces wrong results.' The paper quotes the first half at main.tex:1775-1779 and stops before 'produces wrong results'. Mechanically identical to the observed live-slot C-bind case.

the scoreboard block (btree_fsm_fast.sv:704-720) re-sets an already-set bit with no check; no RTL assertion exists. The paper concedes it at main.tex:1647-1653 ('not by hardware refusal of a second write ... A bug that silently corrupted the allocator would be caught by our assertion harness but not by the fabric') -- and the named assertion harness is absent from the artifact.
the paper's own main.tex:1510-1516: without the GCI retry latch 'the next COMPUTE would read a wrong leaf and produce a wrong root'. Direct verbatim contradiction of Property 2.

scoreboard[0] is forced to 1 at reset (btree_fsm_fast.sv:709) regardless of DMEM[0]'s contents, so a non-identity DMEM[0] is read without complaint. (This is also why 'addr_a -> 0' would be a silent mutation; none of the 54 drew 0.)

no monotonicity check in RTL; zero SVA in the artifact. A 1->1 transition is a no-op, not an error. The paper's remark at main.tex:1018-1021 says 'the fabric's SVA suite flags' it; tb/sva/tb_sva_e2e.sv does not exist in the artifact.
if the gate itself failed, COMPUTE would read an uninitialised slot and proceed. Nothing checks the checker.
a forwarding miss yields a stale operand and a wrong root; no runtime check.
arithmetic error propagates to the root; the fabric never compares against anything.

not a fabric-observable event at all: a nondeterministic compiler either emits another ABI-compliant image (outcome (a), benign) or reduces to one of the classes above. The fabric cannot detect it in principle.
if the watchdog failed to fire, a deadlocked program would simply hang until the testbench loop cap; not a wrong root, but outcome (c)'s diagnostic is lost.

detectable_assumptions.summary_count: Of the fifteen assumptions, four (C-route, F-credit, F-misroute, F-watchdog/invalid-opcode) are provably converted into localised fail-stops, and none of the four has ever been injected. Two (C-bind, C-conn) are detected only when the misbound slot is absent -- observed at 43/54 for C-bind. Nine (C-alpha, C-sw, C-leaf, F-id, F-sb-mono, F-sb-gate, F-fw, F-fadd, F-arb) can pass silently, and for two of them -- C-leaf and F-arb -- the paper's own text or data already says so.

correct_restatement:
Replace Property 2 with a presence-boundary statement and an explicit exclusion list. Recommended wording, drop-in for main.tex:830-843:

  'Under the same assumptions a weaker but useful safety property holds, and its scope is exactly the set of violations that leave some operand absent.

  PROPERTY 2 (Presence-gated fail-stop). Suppose an assumption violation causes some COMPUTE to name a DMEM address whose presence bit is never set -- because a packet was misrouted and dropped (F-misroute), because a credit was lost and the value never arrived (F-credit), because a routing table names an unreachable destination (C-route), or because an operand was bound to an unwritten slot (C-bind, C-conn). Then no instruction retires on the affected PE, F-watchdog fires after WATCHDOG_MAX = 20,000 consecutive non-retiring cycles, and the PE enters P_ERROR recording error_pc and error_state; all_done is never asserted and no root is produced. An invalid opcode raises P_ERROR immediately. The fabric therefore never returns a root in these cases.

  The converse bound is equally explicit. The fabric checks presence, not identity: a COMPUTE whose operands are all present executes, whatever they are. Violations that leave every read address present -- an operand misbound to a live slot (C-bind, C-conn), a corrupted leaf value (C-leaf), a duplicate write to a receive buffer (C-sw), or a violation of F-id, F-sb-mono, F-sb-gate, F-fw, F-fadd or F-arb -- terminate normally with a wrong root. These are discharged before or outside the fabric: C-bind, C-sw and C-leaf by a compile-time post-condition on the emitted image, and all of them by comparison of the final root against the compiler-computed expected value. We do not claim the fabric detects them.'

Evidence sentence to add in Sec. results-invariance, replacing the current '107/107' framing (about 0.15 page, net negative after the property shrinks):

  'The injected-fault campaign separates along exactly this boundary. Of the 54 address-substitution mutants, 43 repointed an operand at a DMEM slot no agent writes; every one of those fail-stopped, the fabric raising P_ERROR with error_pc on each PE, which is the property's outcome (b) observed under injected fault. The remaining mutants, and all 54 leaf-corruption mutants, terminated normally with a wrong root and were caught by the expected-value comparison. Oracle non-vacuity therefore rests on the 6X mutants whose root reached that comparison, not on all 107.'

Downstream edits this forces: abstract ('never a silently wrong output' -> 'never returns a root when an operand never arrives'); Contribution C1 bullet at main.tex:160; Fig. 2's Property-2 subtree (it currently hangs the property off F-misroute/F-arb/F-credit/F-watchdog -- F-arb must be removed, and C-route/C-bind added); the Remark at main.tex:1010-1021 (delete the F-sb-mono/SVA sentence, since no SVA exists); Sec. fail-stop's 'There is no silent-corruption outcome under any configuration we have exercised' at main.tex:1486-1487 (false: 61-65 exercised configurations had exactly that outcome); and either ship or delete the citations to validate_abi.py, validate_routing.py, tb/sva/tb_sva_e2e.sv and tests/mutation/ in Sec. mechanization and the Artifact appendix.

cheapest_adequate_fix.recommended: REMOVE OR NARROW CLAIM + ADD ANALYSIS on data in hand. No new experiment.
cheapest_adequate_fix.why_no_new_experiment: Option (b) in the theme question -- implement the scoreboard 1->1 P_ERROR check plus a hardware operand-binding check and re-run the campaign -- fails the bar on three counts. (i) A hardware operand-binding check is not a small RTL change: the fabric would have to carry tree-node identity in the ISA and in every packet, which changes the ABI the paper is about. (ii) It is not needed: the narrowed property is true, provable by inspection of one always_comb block, and already has 43 injected-fault confirmations. (iii) A Q1 referee will not reject for the absence of a guard the paper explicitly lists as future work (L9) -- referees reject for a property that the paper's own Sec. write-arb contradicts, and that is fixed by deleting eight assumption names.
cheapest_adequate_fix.what_the_analysis_costs: About 20 minutes of Python already written (/tmp/t03/classify_all.py) plus optional confirmatory xsim runs at roughly 2-40 minutes each. The full re-classification of all 54 addr_sub mutants requires no simulation.
cheapest_adequate_fix.harness_patch_before_artifact_release: _mutation_runner.py:257-262 should record a class, not a boolean: `if '[PASS]' in txt: cls='MISSED' elif 'TIMEOUT' in txt: cls='FAILSTOP' elif '[FAIL]' in txt: cls='MISMATCH'`, and it should retain the [ERROR]/[STALL] lines. Three lines. Without it a referee who opens the harness sees the conflation in ten seconds.
cheapest_adequate_fix.page_delta: -0.2 to -0.3 net. The narrowed property is shorter, the Remark at main.tex:1010-1021 loses two sentences, Fig. 2's right-hand cluster shrinks, and the new evidence sentence costs about 0.15 page.

maxp_dense_hc s1000 (8192 leaves, 1024 PEs, PROCEEDS_REMOTE class) was not simulated: the regenerated testbench is 57 MB and elaboration is the same cost that made the sibling run the campaign's only 'no verdict'. Static classification stands; cost to confirm is hours of xelab, not minutes.

The claim that a C-conn violation produces a silently wrong root is supported by the compiler's own docstring and by the mechanically identical live-slot C-bind result, but I did not compile an image with repair_connectivity disabled and simulate it. That would be the direct test; it is cheap (one small instance) if the council wants it, but the narrowed property does not depend on it.
